body:
An attempt to fix #7886 and #9632, with potential API breaking change.

As noted by [ParthSareen](https://github.com/ParthSareen) in https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/8887#issuecomment-2640721896, the current implementation ensures that `content` and `tool_calls` cannot coexist. When no `tool_call` is present, Ollama returns the content as a single chunk.

This PR stream both `tool_calls` and `content`, ensuring `content` stream is available even if no tool call is parsed, which means you'll get `tool_calls` alongside with `content`.

The impact might be minimal, since we can ignore `content` all alone when handling tool call response, same as the current implementation assumes adding tools only when you expect the model to use it, 

Anyway, more input is definitely needed on this change to ensure it addresses the broader range of use cases with minimal side effect.

Demo from MCP client with qwen2.5:0.5b:

body:
Please review official Vertex AI Docs Here: 

https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/model-reference/text-embeddings-api

More specifically it lists a `taskType` parameter: 

> Used to convey intended downstream application to help the model produce better embeddings. If left blank, the default used is RETRIEVAL_QUERY.

As well as an `autoTruncate` parameter:

> When set to true, input text will be truncated. When set to false, an error is returned if the input text is longer than the maximum length supported by the model. Defaults to true.


Currently these are inaccessible via the Vercel AI SDK so I've added them to the settings and updated the implementation of the embedding model for Vertex-AI to be able to pass in these parameters.


Before:

```typescript
const model = vertex.textEmbeddingModel('text-embedding-004', {
  outputDimensionality: 512, // optional, number of dimensions for the embedding
});
```

After:

```typescript
const model = vertex.textEmbeddingModel('text-embedding-004', {
  outputDimensionality: 512, // optional, number of dimensions for the embedding
  taskType: 'RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT', // optional, task type for which embeddings will be used
  autoTruncate: true, // optional, whether to auto-truncate text exceeding token limit
});

```

# Pull Request Description

## Changes Made
This PR adds the following changes:

Add a SolanaFMParser to the SolanaAgentKit. An Action has been added to parse instruction raw data and account raw data in base64 format. The SolanaAgent can decode raw data by taking either a programId and instruction data or a programId and account data as input parameters.
- raw data of instruction for `SolanaParseInstructionTool`.
- raw data of account for `SolanaParseAccountTool`
  
## Implementation Details
This PR includes the implementation of parse instruction data and parse account data from transaction. User(or Agent) can parse base64 encoded data based on the SolanaFMParser library by providing programId and encoded data as a parameters.

Among the agent tools for data parsing, there is a transaction parser that leverages helius API, This feature is available at the transaction level rather than for individual instructions or accounts, and it comes with the limitation of requiring the Helius API Key. The SolanaFMParser introduced in the above PR allows you to decode data for each instruction or account without requiring an additional API key.

Fetch the IDL using the provided programId as the first argument, and decode the data given as the second argument based on that IDL.
If the programId is invalid or the data does not conform to the defined format, throw an error.

If the data is successfully decoded, return the provided programId, the data layout, and the decoded data.

## Transaction executed by agent 
This feature does not generate any transactions on-chain. It is designed to decode the given data.

For the parsing instruction data:

## Description
This PR integrates a new transpiler that converts ASTx nodes into Python’s AST module (ast). Previously, the transpilation was limited to generating Python source code, but now it directly produces Python AST structures, enabling better integration with tools like compile(), exec(), and static analysis frameworks.
Resolves #172 


##  Feature Implementation in `python_ast.py`

I have implemented the following features in **`python_ast.py`** as part of the integration of **ASTx to Python AST transpilation**:

###  Implemented Features  
- **Node Visitor Pattern**: Converted ASTx nodes into Python AST nodes.  
- **Expressions Support**: Implemented `BinaryOp`, `FunctionCall`, `Literals`, and more.  
- **Statements Support**: Added `IfStmt`, `WhileStmt`, `FunctionDef`, etc.  
- **Declarations Handling**: Supported `VariableDeclaration`, `FunctionPrototype`, and more.  
- **Variable Scoping & Function Definitions**: Ensured correct variable tracking across scopes.  

---

###  Next Steps  
 **Review & Validation**: If the current implementation is **validated** and aligns with the project goals, I will proceed to integrate similar changes into **`python.py`** for full transpiler support.  
 **Additional Enhancements**: I am open to feedback for improvements, additional feature requests, or necessary fixes before extending it to **`python.py`**.  

---

Let me know if any modifications or optimizations are required before proceeding further! 🚀  



## Python Memory & Scope Management Features
| Feature                        | Description                                      | Python AST Equivalent                |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Garbage Collection Control** | Detect and manage references dynamically        | `gc.collect()`, `weakref`           |
| **Heap & Stack Analysis**      | Analyze variable memory locations               | `sys._getframe()`                    |
| **Symbol Table Management**    | Directly modify variable scope dynamically      | `symtable` module                     |
| **Dynamic Variable Resolution**| Access variables at runtime                     | `globals()`, `locals()`              |

---

## Low-Level Python Constructs
| Feature                    | Description                                       | Python AST Equivalent                |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Bytecode Manipulation**  | Directly modify Python bytecode at runtime       | `dis.Bytecode()`, `exec()`           |
| **Raw Byte Objects**       | `b'hello'` binary literals                        | `ast.Bytes`                          |
| **Dynamic Metaclasses**    | Modify class behavior dynamically                 | `type("NewClass", (Base,), {})`      |
| **Pointer Arithmetic (via C FFI)** | Interact with memory directly using C functions | `ctypes`, `cffi`                      |

---

## High-Level Functional Programming Features
| Feature                  | Description                                    | Python AST Equivalent                |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Higher-Order Functions** | Functions that take/return other functions   | `ast.Lambda`, `ast.FunctionDef`      |
| **Currying (`functools.partial`)** | Pre-fill function arguments              | `ast.Call(func=partial)`             |
| **Memoization (`lru_cache`)** | Cache function results for efficiency      | `ast.FunctionDef` with `@lru_cache`  |

---

## Machine Learning & Data Science Features
| Feature                      | Description                                      | Python AST Equivalent               |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Lazy Evaluation Pipelines** | Convert expressions to deferred execution        | `dask`, `lazy_eval()`               |
| **Automatic NumPy Vectorization** | Optimize loops for NumPy operations            | `np.vectorize()`                    |
| **Parallel Execution of Expressions** | Convert loops into parallel tasks            | `multiprocessing`, `ast.AsyncFor`   |

---

## AI-Generated Code & LLM Integration
| Feature                       | Description                                       | Python AST Equivalent               |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **AST-Based Code Generation**  | Use AI to generate Python code dynamically       | `openai.ChatGPT()`, `exec(ast.unparse())` |
| **Autonomous Code Refactoring** | Rewrite inefficient code dynamically             | `ast.Module` transformation        |
| **Bug Prediction in Code**     | Use AI to detect potential errors               | `GPT-4 API`, `Linting tools`       |

## Next Steps
- Write unit tests to validate the AST conversion.

- Optimize performance where necessary, especially for large AST structures.

- Document usage examples for developers integrating the new transpiler.

  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.

body:
Original idea:

> We [realised in GETTSIM](https://github.com/iza-institute-of-labor-economics/gettsim/issues/848) that it will often be helpful to work with an object that removes all tree logic, i.e. a dictionary with the following properties
> 1. Keys are qualified absolute names
> 2. Functions in the values only take qualified absolute names as a inputs
> 
> Previously, the function `_qual_name_functions_with_abs_path_args` created precisely this object. This PR renames it to `functions_without_tree_logic` and exposes it.

As it turns out, this grew into something much larger, as much of the logic was duplicated across the various functions. The new strategy that has been possible since the fixation of global namespaces early on is to first convert everything to qualified absolute paths, then work with those not using any tree logic.

body:
This pull request addresses a recurring Heroku deployment error in the GitHub Actions pipeline. After troubleshooting, the deployment issue was resolved by removing the Heroku deployment configuration from the GitHub Actions workflow entirely.

Instead, Heroku's automated deployment and Git tracking features have been enabled to streamline the deployment process. This approach ensures a more reliable and efficient deployment pipeline.

Key changes in this PR:
- Removed Heroku deployment steps from the .github/workflows file.
- Verified Heroku's automated deployment and git tracking are functioning as expected.

This change simplifies the deployment process and helps avoid future conflicts with GitHub Actions.
